extracted.intended_audience: aspiring to intermediate and advanced writers of fiction and memoir (participants in writing workshops / self-directed writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, sentence-to-narrative guidance for writers of fiction and memoir, emphasizing technical command of language, point of view, sound, and revision, with exercises for solo or group practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend to the sound of language as a fundamental component of narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Le Guin lists the sound of language as one of the core topics; chapters include illustrative examples from the global canon and exercises to practice sound. The book emphasizes hearing how language works as a tool of storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Master sentence construction—the shape, rhythm, and function of sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book devotes a chapter to sentence construction and provides exercises. Le Guin also urges familiarity with grammatical vocabulary so writers can identify and fix sentence problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and choose point of view as a central narrative decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point of view is named among the fundamental components of narrative addressed in the chapters; examples and commentary illustrate POV choices and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with grammatical terminology (writer's tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the technical vocabulary of speech and writing (subject, predicate, object, adjective, adverb, tenses) to describe and improve sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Le Guin argues that without the names of grammatical tools a writer cannot say what's right or wrong in a sentence; she encourages getting familiar with these terms to be able to play with language freely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises and deliberate practice (solo or group)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured exercises to practice craft, either alone or in a group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chapter combines illustrative examples with an exercise that the writer can do solo or in a group. The revised edition updates and improves exercises, emphasizing practice as a route to improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working in writing groups (real and online)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop skills for productive participation in writing groups, including online groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book offers a comprehensive guide to working in writing groups, both actual and online, as part of its practical apparatus for writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention and self-discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate attention and self-discipline as necessary habits for improving craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Le Guin states writing is a craft that can be learned through attention and self-discipline; she uses the metaphor of weighing words to distinguish weak ('Styrofoam') from strong ('heavy gold') wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and iterative improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace revision and rewriting as essential to improving writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book itself is a revised and rewritten edition based on reader feedback; Le Guin's approach implies iterative improvement—revising exercises and topics to better teach craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrative examples from the global canon
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn craft through close attention to examples drawn from world literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chapter combines illustrative examples from the global canon with commentary, using existing texts to show craft principles in action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation to contemporary/electronic contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply craft principles in the context of modern electronic communication and the changing publishing landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Le Guin updated the book to address the challenges and opportunities of the modern era and the age of electronic communication, signaling attention to how medium and market affect practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make prose 'seaworthy'—robustness and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure writing is robust, clear, and resistant to common failures (avoid 'capsizing' or 'hitting an iceberg').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a nautical metaphor, Le Guin offers 'basic ways to make her seaworthy'—practical techniques to keep prose from failing; the book frames craft as methods to prevent common breakdowns in writing.
